skill_drafts.name: Vector Space Document Similarity Scoring
skill_drafts.description: Compute similarity between two documents by normalizing term frequency vectors and computing their dot product. Returns a scalar similarity score suitable for ranking or comparing document relevance.
applicable_signals: term frequency vectors are computed and normalized
documents are represented in the same vector space
comparison is between exactly two documents
contraindications: documents are not yet vectorized or term frequencies are not available
only categorical or boolean relevance judgment is needed
vectors are not normalized to unit length
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Normalize term frequency vector for document 1 by dividing each component by the Euclidean length |v(d1)|'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Normalize term frequency vector for document 2 by dividing each component by the Euclidean length |v(d2)|'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Compute dot product of the two normalized vectors: sim(d1, d2) = v(d1) · v(d2)'}
triggers: need to rank or compare two documents
have term frequency vectors available for both documents
require a continuous similarity score for relevance assessment
constraints: both input vectors must be normalized by their Euclidean length
vectors must represent the same set of terms or term dimensions
output score is bounded between 0 and 1 for normalized vectors
cautions: ensure normalization is applied before dot product to maintain score comparability
verify that both documents are represented in the same vector space (same term vocabulary)
output_contract: A scalar similarity score between 0 and 1 representing the cosine similarity of the two normalized document vectors. Score of 1 indicates identical documents; score of 0 indicates orthogonal (completely dissimilar) documents.

metadata.prompt: Given two documents represented as normalized term frequency vectors, compute their similarity by taking the dot product of the vectors. Normalize each vector by its Euclidean length before computing the dot product to ensure scores are comparable across document pairs.

skill_drafts.name: Euclidean Normalization of Term Frequency Vectors
skill_drafts.description: Normalize raw term frequency vectors by dividing each component by the vector's Euclidean norm. Use before computing dot-product similarity to ensure scale-invariant comparison across documents of different lengths.
applicable_signals: need to compare documents of different lengths fairly
preparing vectors for cosine similarity or dot-product scoring
contraindications: Only raw frequency ranking is acceptable without normalization
Scale-invariance is not required for the use case
workflow_steps: {'step': 1, 'action': 'Extract raw term frequency vector ~v(d) from document', 'detail': 'Collect term occurrence counts for all terms in vocabulary'}
{'step': 2, 'action': 'Compute Euclidean norm', 'detail': 'Calculate |~v(d)| = sqrt(sum of v_i^2 for all components v_i)'}
{'step': 3, 'action': 'Normalize each component', 'detail': 'Divide each component by the norm: v_i_normalized = v_i / |~v(d)|'}
{'step': 4, 'action': 'Verify unit length', 'detail': 'Confirm that the normalized vector has Euclidean length 1.0 (within numerical precision)'}
triggers: Raw term frequency counts are available for one or more documents
Documents have different lengths and need fair comparison
Dot-product similarity will be computed downstream
constraints: Input must be a valid term frequency vector with non-negative numeric components
Euclidean norm must be non-zero (empty or zero-only vectors cannot be normalized)
cautions: Ensure all term frequencies are non-negative before normalization
Handle zero-norm vectors explicitly (e.g., documents with no terms) to avoid division by zero
output_contract: A normalized vector with unit Euclidean length, ready for dot-product similarity computation. Each component is scaled such that the vector's magnitude equals 1.0.

examples.input: Raw term frequency vector for document: affection=115, jealous=10, gossip=2
examples.output: Normalized vector: affection≈0.996, jealous≈0.087, gossip≈0.017 (unit Euclidean length)
examples.notes: Normalization makes documents of different lengths comparable; longer documents no longer dominate similarity scores

metadata.prompt: Given a raw term frequency vector ~v(d) with components for each term in a document, compute the Euclidean norm |~v(d)| = sqrt(sum of squared components). Divide each component by this norm to produce a unit-length normalized vector ~v(d) / |~v(d)|. This normalized vector is then suitable for dot-product similarity computation.

skill_drafts.name: Term Frequency Extraction and Tabulation
skill_drafts.description: Count occurrences of selected terms across a document collection and organize results into a term-document frequency matrix. This is the foundational data collection step for vector space model construction, producing raw frequency counts that serve as input to downstream weighting and normalization workflows.
applicable_signals: Term vocabulary has been selected or extracted
Downstream task requires term frequency input
contraindications: Only boolean presence/absence of terms is needed (use simpler binary indexing instead)
Term frequencies are not available or not relevant to the task
Documents are too large or numerous for manual frequency counting without automated tools
workflow_steps: Define the term vocabulary (list of terms to count)
Initialize a matrix with terms as rows and documents as columns
For each document, scan and count occurrences of each term
Record counts in the corresponding matrix cell
Verify matrix completeness: all cells populated, no missing documents or terms
triggers: Starting a vector space model workflow
Have a raw document collection and a defined term list
Need to prepare data for tf-idf weighting or vector normalization
constraints: All selected terms must be consistently counted across all documents
Frequency counts must be non-negative integers
Matrix must include all documents in the collection and all terms in the vocabulary
cautions: Ensure term matching is case-consistent and handles stemming/normalization uniformly if required
Verify that the term list is complete before beginning counting to avoid incomplete matrices
Document the counting methodology (e.g., whole-word match vs. substring) for reproducibility
output_contract: A term-document frequency matrix with raw occurrence counts (rows = terms, columns = documents, cells = non-negative integer counts). Format example: term 'affection' appears 115 times in document SaS, 58 times in PaP, 20 times in WH. This matrix is ready for downstream tf-idf weighting, normalization, or vector space model construction.

examples.input: Document collection: three novels (Sense and Sensibility, Pride and Prejudice, Wuthering Heights); term list: [affection, jealous, gossip]
examples.notes: Raw counts organized by term and document; ready for normalization or weighting

metadata.prompt: For each term in your selected term list, count its occurrences in each document in the collection. Organize counts into a matrix with terms as rows and documents as columns. Ensure all documents are represented and all term counts are recorded as non-negative integers. This matrix becomes the input for tf-idf weighting and vector normalization.
